formats.key: createTimelock(((address storageToken, uint256 amountOutMin, uint256 deadline) timelockETHSwap, (address tokenAddress, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC20, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id)[] timelockERC721, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC1155, uint256 duration, string name) timelockRegular)
effects: The signer sends msg.value ETH. The router wraps it 1:1 to WETH, or swaps it on Uniswap V2 for storageToken with at least amountOutMin. The output goes to the TimelockERC20 vault.
Each listed ERC-20 amount is pulled from the signer with transferFrom into the TimelockERC20 vault. This uses the signer's existing allowance to the router.
Each listed ERC-721 token id is pulled from the signer into the TimelockERC721 vault.
Each listed ERC-1155 id and amount is pulled from the signer into the TimelockERC1155 vault.
A timelock with a new id is created. The signer owns it, it is locked for `duration`, and the swapped token is marked to be paid out as ETH.
formats.shown: "Create timelock" with the ETH sent, the storage token, the swap minimum and deadline, each ERC-20 amount with its token, each NFT and ERC-1155 item, and the lock duration.

findings.title: createTimelock labels amountOutMin 'Swap min (not WETH)' but still shows it as a WETH amount
findings.evidence: Case 1 shows 'Swap min (not WETH)': '0.3 WETH'. TimeLockRouter._executeEthSwapForToken: `if (timelockETHSwap.storageToken == weth) { IWETH(weth).deposit{value: msg.value}(); ... return (weth, msg.value); }`, so amountOutMin is ignored for WETH.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Minimum received from swap'. In tests, use amountOutMin 0 for the WETH path, or note that a WETH wrap is always 1:1.

findings.title: createTimelock hides the swap minimum when it is 0, so a swap with no slippage bound shows no minimum
findings.evidence: Descriptor field amountOutMin has `visible: {ifNotIn: [0]}`. TimeLockRouter._executeEthSwapForToken passes amountOutMin to `swapExactETHForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens`, and 0 there means no bound.
findings.fix: Always show amountOutMin while storageToken is set, or show the message 'No minimum' for 0.

findings.title: createTimelock shows 'ETH held as' as a raw hex address instead of the token name
findings.evidence: Case 1: 'ETH held as': '0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2'. The field uses addressName with sources ['local'] only.
findings.fix: Use a token-aware source so WETH and other storage tokens resolve to a ticker, or state the token in the swap-min amount only.

findings.title: createTimelock intent does not say the assets are locked and cannot be withdrawn until the duration ends
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: 'Create timelock', no interpolatedIntent. TimeLockRouter._createTimelockRegular moves all listed assets out of the signer's wallet into the vaults for `duration`.
findings.fix: Use the intent 'Lock assets for a fixed time' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Lock assets for {duration}'.

findings.title: createTimelock shows the duration as hours, '8760:00:00', not as days or years
findings.evidence: Case 0: 'Locked for': '8760:00:00'. The field uses `format: duration`.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can render years. You can add the length in words to the label, such as 'Locked for (h:m:s)'.

findings.title: createTimelock tests do not cover ERC-721, ERC-1155 or a non-WETH swap with a real minimum
findings.evidence: Cases 0 and 1 only lock USDC or wrap ETH to WETH. The bundled NFT and item fields and the Uniswap swap branch in _executeEthSwapForToken are not exercised.
findings.fix: Add cases with an NFT, an ERC-1155 item, and storageToken set to a non-WETH token with amountOutMin above 0.

formats.key: createSoftTimelock(((address storageToken, uint256 amountOutMin, uint256 deadline) timelockETHSwap, (address tokenAddress, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC20, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id)[] timelockERC721, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC1155, uint256 bufferTime, string name) timelockSoft)
effects: The signer sends msg.value ETH. The router wraps it to WETH or swaps it on Uniswap V2 for storageToken with at least amountOutMin, into the TimelockERC20 vault.
The listed ERC-20 amounts, ERC-721 ids and ERC-1155 ids and amounts are pulled from the signer into the vaults.
A soft timelock is created that the signer owns. It has no end date: the signer must call unlockSoftTimelock and then wait bufferTime before withdrawing.
formats.shown: "Create soft timelock" with the ETH sent, the storage token, the swap minimum and deadline, the token amounts, NFTs and items, and 'Unlock delay'.

findings.title: createSoftTimelock intent 'Create soft timelock' does not explain that the assets stay locked until an unlock plus delay
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: 'Create soft timelock'. TimeLockRouter._createSoftTimelock uses bufferTime only. Release needs unlockSoftTimelock and then the delay.
findings.fix: Use the intent 'Lock assets until you unlock + delay' and an interpolatedIntent with {bufferTime}.

findings.title: createSoftTimelock labels amountOutMin 'Swap min (not WETH)' but shows it as a WETH amount
findings.evidence: Case 3: 'Swap min (not WETH)': '0.3 WETH'. _executeEthSwapForToken ignores amountOutMin when storageToken == weth.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Minimum received from swap'.

findings.title: createSoftTimelock hides the swap minimum when it is 0, so a swap with no slippage bound shows no minimum
findings.evidence: Field amountOutMin has `visible: {ifNotIn: [0]}`. _executeEthSwapForToken passes it as the Uniswap amountOutMin.
findings.fix: Always show amountOutMin while storageToken is set, or show the message 'No minimum' for 0.

findings.title: createSoftTimelock shows the storage token as a raw hex address
findings.evidence: Case 3: 'ETH held as': '0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2'.
findings.fix: Resolve the storage token to its ticker.

findings.title: createSoftTimelock tests do not cover NFTs, ERC-1155 items or a real Uniswap swap
findings.evidence: Cases 2 and 3 only lock USDC or wrap ETH to WETH.
findings.fix: Add cases with an NFT, an ERC-1155 item and a non-WETH storage token.

formats.key: createTimelockedGift(((address storageToken, uint256 amountOutMin, uint256 deadline) timelockETHSwap, (address tokenAddress, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC20, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id)[] timelockERC721, (address tokenAddress, uint256 id, uint256 amount)[] timelockERC1155, uint256 duration, address recipient, string name, string giftName) timelockGift)
effects: The signer sends msg.value ETH. The router wraps it or swaps it for storageToken with at least amountOutMin, into the TimelockERC20 vault.
The listed ERC-20, ERC-721 and ERC-1155 assets are pulled from the signer into the vaults.
A gift timelock is created. `recipient` can withdraw the assets after `duration`, and the signer stays recorded as owner.
When a consent verifier is set, the router records that the signer accepts the active terms for this timelock id (consentVerifier.recordConsent).
formats.shown: "Seal gift and accept terms" with the ETH sent, the storage token, the swap minimum and deadline, the token amounts, NFTs and items, 'Opens after' and the recipient.

findings.title: createTimelockedGift intent does not name the recipient or say the assets leave the signer
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: 'Seal gift and accept terms', no interpolatedIntent. _createTimelockedGift passes timelockGift.recipient to the vaults as the party who can withdraw.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Gift locked assets to {recipient}, opens after {duration}'.

findings.title: createTimelockedGift records acceptance of terms that the screen cannot show
findings.evidence: TimeLockRouter._createTimelockedGift: `consentVerifier.recordConsent(msg.sender, timelockCounter);`. The terms live in the verifier's storage.
findings.fix: Point the signer to the terms URL in metadata.info, or keep it as is.

findings.title: createTimelockedGift hides the swap minimum when it is 0, so a swap with no slippage bound shows no minimum
findings.evidence: Field amountOutMin has `visible: {ifNotIn: [0]}`. _executeEthSwapForToken passes it to Uniswap.
findings.fix: Always show amountOutMin while storageToken is set, or show the message 'No minimum' for 0.

findings.title: createTimelockedGift labels amountOutMin 'Swap min (not WETH)' but shows '0.3 WETH'
findings.evidence: Case 5: 'Swap min (not WETH)': '0.3 WETH'.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Minimum received from swap'.

findings.title: createTimelockedGift shows the storage token as a raw hex address
findings.evidence: Case 5: 'ETH held as': '0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2'.
findings.fix: Resolve the storage token to its ticker.

effects: Starts the unlock countdown (bufferTime) for soft timelock `id` in the ERC-20, ERC-721 and ERC-1155 vaults, with the signer as caller. After the delay the owner can withdraw. Nothing moves in this call.
formats.shown: "Start soft timelock countdown" with the timelock id.

findings.title: unlockSoftTimelock shows only the id, not the locked assets or the delay, which live in vault storage
findings.evidence: TimeLockRouter.unlockSoftTimelock: `timelockERC20Contract.unlockSoftTimelock(id, msg.sender); ...`. The descriptor field is id with format raw.

effects: Each vault releases the assets of timelock `id` to the signer (msg.sender), if the signer is the owner or the recipient and the lock has expired.
The ERC-20 vault is called with skipSwap = false, so a swapped storage token is converted back to ETH before payout. The bound of that conversion is in unverified vault code.
formats.shown: "Withdraw from timelock" with the timelock id.

findings.title: withdraw(id) does not say that swapped tokens are converted back to ETH
findings.evidence: TimeLockRouter.withdraw(uint256): `timelockERC20Contract.withdraw(id, msg.sender, false);`. Descriptor intent: 'Withdraw from timelock'.
findings.fix: Use the intent 'Withdraw timelock, swapped tokens as ETH'.

findings.title: withdraw(id) cannot show the assets or the amounts received, because they are stored in the vaults
findings.evidence: withdraw(uint256) passes only id and msg.sender to the vaults. The descriptor shows only 'Timelock' raw.

effects: Each vault releases the assets of timelock `id` to the signer.
When skipSwap is false, the ERC-20 vault converts the swapped storage token back to ETH. When it is true, the signer receives the token itself.
formats.shown: "Withdraw from timelock" with the timelock id and 'Skip ETH conversion' as raw true or false.

findings.title: withdraw(id, skipSwap) shows the payout choice as a raw boolean under a negative label
findings.evidence: Descriptor field skipSwap: label 'Skip ETH conversion', format raw. Cases 8 and 9 render 'true' and 'false'. TimeLockRouter.withdraw(uint256,bool) passes skipSwap to timelockERC20Contract.withdraw.
findings.fix: Map the bool with an enum: true -> 'Keep token', false -> 'Convert to ETH'. Use the label 'Receive swapped asset as'.

findings.title: withdraw(id, skipSwap) cannot show the assets or amounts received, which are stored in the vaults
findings.evidence: withdraw(uint256,bool) passes only id, msg.sender and skipSwap to the vaults.

couldNotCheck: The TimelockERC20, TimelockERC721 and TimelockERC1155 vault contracts are not in the directory. Their addresses are in router storage and the source is omitted. They hold createTimelock/createSoftTimelock/createTimelockedGift recording, the unlockSoftTimelock logic, withdraw payout, the token-to-ETH reconversion and its slippage bound, and any creator rights over a gift.
The consentVerifier (IEIP712LegacyVerifier) called by createTimelockedGift is not in the directory, so what recordConsent binds the signer to cannot be checked.
